error.network.bridge.modem: A modem does not lead to the home network, so it cannot be added to the bridge.
error.network.bridge.already: This interface is a bridge or is in one already.
error.network.bridge.outside: This interface is marked as the outside network: the home network is not there.
error.network.bridge.notNm: This interface is not managed by NetworkManager: hand it over to NetworkManager first.
error.network.bridge.noAddress: This interface has no address, so it is not connected to the home network.
error.network.bridge.inUse: Containers and virtual machines are in the home network: {names}. Move them to Hata's own network first.
error.network.bridge.port: This card is part of the home-network bridge and uses the bridge's address: change it on the bridge.
activity.network.bridged: {target} added to the home-network bridge for containers
activity.network.unbridged: Home-network bridge removed, {target} has its own address again
bridge.is: Home-network bridge for containers and virtual machines. Network card in it: {ports}.
bridge.portOf: Part of the bridge {bridge}; uses the bridge's address.
bridge.title: Containers in the home network
bridge.lead: The server's network card is put into a bridge, like vmbr0 in Proxmox. Containers and virtual machines attached to it are on the home network, alongside the server.
bridge.what.router: Each gets an address from the router and appears on the home network as a separate device, reachable at its own address on its usual ports.
bridge.what.card: The server keeps its address: the bridge takes over the card's settings and MAC address, so the router still recognises it.
bridge.what.nat: Hata's own network (behind the server) stays: each container can be on either one.
bridge.what.wifi: Only a wired card can be added to a bridge, not Wi-Fi.
bridge.needsNm: NetworkManager is needed: install it in Network → Connections.
bridge.cardHint: The one that leads to the home network.
bridge.noCard: No card here can be added to a bridge.
bridge.how: Hata makes the NetworkManager profiles “hata-{bridge}” (the bridge) and “hata-{bridge}-<card>” (the card in it); the card's own profile is switched off and kept. The connection drops for a few seconds.
bridge.apartLead: {card} gets its own profile back, with the address settings the bridge has now. Containers on the home network have to be moved to Hata's own network first.
incus.net.title: Network
incus.net.make: Connect containers to the home network…
incus.net.on: New containers and virtual machines join the home network (bridge {bridge}, the server's address there is {address}) unless you choose otherwise; each can be moved between it and Hata's own network.
incus.net.off: Containers and virtual machines are on Hata's own network ({network}): they reach the internet through the server, but cannot be reached from the home network. As in Proxmox, they can be on the home network instead, with addresses from the router.
incus.net.home: Home network — an address from the router
incus.net.private: Hata's own network — inside the server
incus.net.label: Network
incus.net.hint: On the home network it is a separate device, reachable at its own address. On Hata's own network only the server can reach it.
incus.net.none: It will be on Hata's own network, inside the server.
incus.net.now.home: It is in the home network now.
incus.net.now.private: It is on Hata's own network now.
incus.net.now.other: It is on a network Hata did not make.
incus.net.to.home: It will be moved to the home network.
incus.net.to.private: It will be moved to Hata's own network, inside the server.
incus.net.address: It gets an address from the other network; its MAC address stays, so the router may give the same one each time.
incus.net.client: Hata's client inside switches to the server's address on the other network and reconnects as the same computer.
incus.net.open: On the home network every device can reach it directly: make sure the services it runs are protected by a password.
error.containers.network.noBridge: There is no home-network bridge, or it has no address: create it in Network → Connections.
incus.bad.network: Choose a network from the list.
names.title: Names for other services
names.lead: Containers and virtual machines of this server and of Proxmox, computers, their apps or any address on the home network can have a name under the domain (a subdomain) too. Hata forwards requests to the given address and port, as it does for an app — with Hata's certificate and, if you choose, Hata's sign-in in front.
names.noDomain: There is no domain to give names under: in Network → Addresses and HTTPS, turn on the name on the home network or set a domain for HTTPS.
names.col.name: Name
names.label: Name
names.labelHint: Lowercase Latin letters, digits and hyphens.
names.group.containers: Containers and virtual machines of this server
names.hostHint: An IP address or a host name of the home network, without the port.
names.portHint: The port of the target's web page.
names.httpsHint: Like Proxmox's page on port 8006. The target's certificate is not checked, as it is usually self-signed.
names.protect: Only for those signed in to Hata
names.protectHint: Whoever is not signed in is sent to Hata's sign-in page first.
error.domains.badLabel: A name consists of lowercase Latin letters, digits and hyphens, and cannot start or end with a hyphen.
error.domains.taken: The name {label} is already taken by an app or another name.
error.domains.badTarget: Choose what the name leads to; an address is an IP address or a host name without a port.
error.domains.badPort: A port is a number from 1 to 65535.
error.domains.away.noContainer: This container or virtual machine is not on the server any more.
error.domains.away.noGuest: This container or VM is not on the Proxmox server any more.
error.domains.away.noMachine: This computer is not connected to Hata any more.
error.domains.away.machineAway: The computer is not connected right now.
error.domains.away.noAddress: The target has no address right now: it may be stopped.
names.signedInApp: Signed-in users only, as set for the app
ports.title: Port forwarding
ports.lead: A port of this server forwarded to a container, a virtual machine (here or on Proxmox), a computer or any address: SSH to a container, a database, a game server. For a container of this server Incus's own proxy does it (and keeps working while Hata restarts); everything else is forwarded by Hata. The target sees connections as coming from this server.
ports.outsideToo: Home network and the outside network
ports.dialogLead: Connections to this port of the server are forwarded to the target's port.
ports.portHint: Must not be in use by an app or by Hata.
ports.outside: Open on the outside network too
ports.outsideHint: Only matters for an interface marked as the outside network in Network → Connections: otherwise the router decides what comes in from outside.
error.ports.badPort: A port is a number from 1 to 65535.
error.ports.taken: Port {port} is already in use: by another forwarding, or by Hata itself.
error.ports.busy: Port {port} is already in use by another program on this server.
dns.title: Hata as the DNS server of the home network
dns.lead: Devices that use Hata as their DNS server get the home-network name and every name under it — the apps' names and those from Network → Addresses and HTTPS — straight from Hata. Everything else comes from the servers chosen below and is cached for as long as they allow. Only devices on private networks are answered.
dns.what.router: If the router cannot point every subdomain at Hata, it only has to hand Hata out as the DNS server.
dns.what.split: When Hata serves HTTPS itself, its domain opens directly at home, without a trip through the internet.
dns.what.wg: Devices connected over WireGuard get the names too.
dns.failedHolder: Cannot listen on {address}: port 53 is in use by {holder}. Stop that program, or turn Hata's DNS server off and leave DNS to it.
dns.youUse: This device ({address}) uses Hata's DNS: last query at {when}.
dns.youDont: This device ({address}) has not used Hata's DNS yet: it uses another DNS server.
dns.routerTitle: To make every device use it
dns.router: In the router's settings of the home network (DHCP), set the DNS server to {address}. Devices take it when they renew their address — or at once after reconnecting.
dns.routerOne: Make Hata the only DNS server: with a second one, devices pick either at random, and Hata's names then work only some of the time. While Hata is off, devices at home cannot resolve any names, so websites do not open either — put the router's own DNS back in that case.
dns.upLead: Names Hata does not answer itself are looked up at these servers.
dns.up.system: The same as this server uses
dns.upSystem: Now: {list}. Hata's own address is never used — if the router hands out Hata, Quad9 and Cloudflare are used instead.
dns.dohHint: Queries are sent encrypted to port 853: neither your internet provider nor anyone in between sees which names are looked up.
dns.serversHint: IP addresses, or https://…/dns-query for DNS over HTTPS; one per line. A DoH server given by host name itself needs DNS to be found.
dns.looping: These servers send queries back to Hata (for example, a router that itself uses Hata), so they are skipped: {list}.
dns.namesLead: Hata answers these itself, without the upstream servers.
dns.ownDomain: The domain of Hata and every name one level under it
dns.noDomains: Neither the name on the home network nor a domain served by Hata is set.
dns.usage: Queries since start: {queries}. Answered locally: {own}, from cache: {cached}, sent upstream: {upstream}, failed: {failed}, refused: {refused}. Cached answers: {kept}.
dns.offLead: Devices that use Hata as their DNS server stop getting answers: put the router's own DNS server back in its settings first, or devices at home cannot resolve any names and websites do not open. WireGuard devices whose file was made while the DNS server was on use it too: give them a new file.
error.dns.badRecord: A record needs a name and an IPv4 or IPv6 address.
attention.dns.port.title: The DNS server cannot listen on {address}
attention.dns.port.text: Port 53 on that address is in use by {holder}. Devices that use Hata's DNS at that address get no answers.
attention.dns.upstream.title: The upstream DNS servers do not answer
attention.dns.upstream.text: No upstream DNS server has answered for two minutes: at home, sites and services do not open by name, except Hata's own names.
wildcard.title: Wildcard certificate
wildcard.lead: One certificate for the domain and every name one level under it (*.domain). A new name works at once, and the names of your services do not appear in the public certificate logs. Let's Encrypt issues such a certificate only after checking a TXT record in the domain's DNS: choose who adds it; renewals work the same way.
wildcard.via.off: Nobody — a separate certificate for each name
wildcard.via.api: Hata, through the DNS provider's API
wildcard.how.cloudflare: My Profile → API Tokens: a token with Zone → DNS → Edit and Zone → Zone → Read for this domain.
wildcard.how.desec: Token management in your deSEC account.
wildcard.how.duckdns: The token at the top of your DuckDNS page. DuckDNS keeps one TXT value, so the two checks go one after the other and take a little over a minute.
wildcard.how.hetzner: Hetzner Console → the project → Security → API tokens, with read and write. Zones still on the old DNS Console have to be moved to the Console first.
wildcard.how.digitalocean: API → Tokens: a token with the domain scopes read, create and delete.
wildcard.how.gandi: Account → Authentication options → personal access token with the right to manage domain technical configurations.
wildcard.how.route53: An IAM user's key with route53:ListHostedZonesByName and route53:ChangeResourceRecordSets.
wildcard.delegateLead: Add these two records at your DNS provider, once. After that Let's Encrypt checks the record with Hata itself.
wildcard.delegatePort: Port 53 (UDP and TCP) has to reach this server from the internet: forward it on the router. On the outside Hata answers only about this one name. Behind a provider's shared address (CGNAT) this method does not work.
wildcard.dnsNeeded: Turn the DNS server on first
wildcard.manualLead: When a certificate is due, Hata shows the TXT record and waits until you add it. This repeats at every renewal, about every two months; “Needs attention” reminds you.
wildcard.manualAll: If there are two values, add both under the same name. Press the button once they are added.
wildcard.manualGoing: Checking the record, then requesting the certificate…
error.wildcard.badWay: Choose a way from the list.
error.wildcard.needAcme: Hata has to serve HTTPS itself, with a domain, for this.
error.wildcard.dnsOff: Turn the DNS server on first.
error.wildcard.nothingWaits: No DNS record is expected right now.
activity.https.wildcardOff: Wildcard certificate turned off for {target}: a certificate per name again
attention.https.manual.title: The certificate is waiting for a DNS record
attention.https.manual.text: A TXT record at {name} has to be added by hand: Network → Addresses and HTTPS shows it.
attention.https.wildcardFailed.title: No certificate for *.{domain}
wildcard.certificatesLead: One certificate for the domain and every name under it, renewed a month before it expires.
adblock.title: Ad blocking
adblock.lead: Hata's DNS server blocks the domains on the lists you choose for every device that uses it: ads and trackers disappear in apps and on TVs too, where a browser extension cannot help. Pi-hole and AdGuard lists work as they are.
adblock.nothingYet: Nothing is blocked yet: add a list or a rule of your own below.
adblock.serverOff: Hata's DNS server is off, so nothing is blocked.
adblock.nobodyAsks: No device uses Hata's DNS yet: nothing is blocked until the router hands Hata out as the DNS server.
adblock.today: In the last 24 hours: {questions} queries, {blocked} blocked ({share}%).
adblock.chart.title: Queries per hour
adblock.modeHint: Most apps stop trying at once with either. If an app keeps retrying, choose the other one.
adblock.memoryHint: 8 bytes per domain. Hata as a whole uses {process}.
adblock.updateHint: Only lists that have changed are downloaded again.
adblock.knownLead: Maintained by their authors. A bigger list blocks more, but sometimes also something you need: start with one.
adblock.list.none: No lists yet: Hata adds none by default.
adblock.list.chooseOne: Tick a list or enter an address.
adblock.list.urlHint: A hosts file, a plain list of domains, or AdGuard syntax: the format is detected automatically.
adblock.list.name: Name
adblock.list.exceptionsTick: This is a list of exceptions
adblock.list.exceptionsHint: Domains on it are allowed even if another list blocks them.
adblock.list.waiting: Will be downloaded once blocking is turned on
adblock.list.failed: Could not download: {error}. What was downloaded before stays in use.
adblock.list.removeLead: Domains blocked only by this list will no longer be blocked.
adblock.ownLead: One rule per line, in any of the formats. They take priority over every list.
adblock.own.notDns: this is for a browser: a DNS server cannot act on it
adblock.own.cosmetic: this hides parts of a page: only a browser can do that
adblock.own.broken: not recognised, or a regular expression that could take too long
adblock.syntax.sub: the domain and all its subdomains
adblock.syntax.exact: only this domain; a plain example.com or a hosts line does the same
adblock.syntax.regex: a regular expression, as in Pi-hole
adblock.syntax.important: takes priority over exceptions in the lists
adblock.syntax.client: only for this address, network or device name; ~ means all but it
adblock.syntax.rewrite: answer with this address, domain or NXDOMAIN instead
adblock.syntax.badfilter: disables the same rule in any list
adblock.log.keepHint: The last 5000 queries, in memory only and visible to administrators only: the log shows what each device visits. When turned off, it is erased at once.
adblock.log.off: The query log is off: turn it on below.
adblock.check.none: No rule matches {name}: it is not blocked.
adblock.col.name: Domain
adblock.devicesLead: A device is identified by its IP address, so reserve a fixed address for it in the router before naming it or turning blocking off for it. The name can be used in $client.
adblock.devicesNone: No device has used Hata's DNS yet.
adblock.device.name: Name

adblock.left.regexOption: A regular expression with an option Hata does not support:
adblock.left.clientKind: A device identified by something other than an address:
adblock.left.groups: Groups (here a rule itself says who it applies to, with $client):
adblock.left.upstreamDomain: A server for certain domains only:
adblock.left.upstreamKind: A server with a protocol Hata does not support:
adblock.left.rewriteKeep: A rewrite that keeps what the DNS server answers:
adblock.left.customIp: Blocking with a custom address: 0.0.0.0 is used here.

remote.signOutTitle: Sign this server out of Tailscale?
remote.signOutLead: The server leaves your Tailscale network; to join again you will have to sign in by a link. If this page is open over Tailscale, it stops responding.
wg.out.forgetLead: The tunnel is closed, and the configuration you pasted, with its private key, is deleted from this server. To connect again you will need that file.
incus.snap.restoreLead: Everything that changed in {instance} after this snapshot is lost. If it is running, it restarts.
incus.snap.removeLead: The snapshot cannot be restored once deleted, and {instance} can no longer be returned to this point. The current state of {instance} does not change.
passkey.removeLead: The device it is on can no longer sign in with it. Your password keeps working.
home.removeLinkLead: The link is not saved anywhere else: its name and the address {url} will be lost.
raid.repairLead: The disks of this array differ in places. Repair makes them identical by overwriting one copy with the other. It cannot tell which copy was right, so the overwritten data is lost. Make a backup first.
raid.clearLead: The record of these errors is deleted and they are no longer shown. Nothing on the disks changes, and a failing disk keeps failing.
raid.forgetTitle: Clear the result of the last check of {name}?
raid.forgetLead: The mismatches it found are no longer shown. Nothing on the disks changes; the next check will count them again.
tools.removeLeadIncus: Incus is removed with everything it holds: images, disc images, storage places and networks are deleted, along with its folders. A later install starts from scratch.
backup.deleteLead: It cannot be restored afterwards, and it is deleted from the second copy on another machine too. Undoing an update may need it.
wg.offLead: Every device connected through it is disconnected. If this page is open over WireGuard, it stops responding, and the server can be reached from outside only another way.
remote.offLead: The server leaves the Tailscale network until Tailscale is switched on again. If this page is open over Tailscale, it stops responding, and you will need another way to the server to switch it back on.
outside.homeLead: Hata's firewall is turned off on this interface: Hata's pages, shared folders and Docker's published ports answer anyone who can reach it. On a provider's cable that means the whole internet.
network.roleOffLead: It is the main connection now. Without a backup connection the server loses the internet at once and can no longer be reached from outside. The home network keeps working.
array.syncLead: The parity will no longer cover them, and “Restore them” will no longer work.
machines.people.unshareLead: Users lose access to it, and the rights set for each of them are deleted. The files stay on the computer.
assistant.forgetLead: The chat cannot be restored. What the assistant has already done is not undone.
app.login.notFound: The password is not in the log yet. If the app has just started, wait a moment and try again. If you have set your own password, the app no longer writes one to the log.
app.login.default: The app's default sign-in. It stops working once you change it in the app.
app.login.settings: As set in the app's settings in Hata. If it was changed inside the app itself, Hata does not know the new one.
app.login.log: The app writes the password to its log. Every time it is shown here is recorded in the activity log.
app.login.first-visit: The app asks you to create an account the first time you open it.
app.login.none: The app has no sign-in of its own.

tv.title: TV
tv.lead: A media player on the TV or monitor connected to this server: films, music and photos from its folders, controlled from this page or with a remote.
tv.noScreen: No TV or monitor is detected on any output. Check the cable and that the TV is set to the right input.
tv.noOutput: This server has no video output (virtual machines and containers often have none).
tv.remotesHint: A keyboard, mouse or remote connected to the server controls the player directly. On remotes for Android boxes the OK and Menu buttons are remapped so that Kodi understands them. Power and sleep buttons on connected keyboards and remotes are disabled: otherwise they would shut the whole server down. The TV's own remote works only if the server's HDMI port supports CEC; most mini PCs do not.
tv.remotesHint.browser: A mouse or an air-mouse remote plugged into the server moves the pointer on the page and clicks; a keyboard types into it. The remote's “back” goes a page back, “home” gives the screen back. The power and sleep buttons of plugged-in keyboards and remotes are turned off: they would shut the whole server down.
tv.needsShort: The player is Kodi, a free media centre. Install it from the TV page.
tv.needsLead: The player is Kodi, a free media centre. With its graphics and video decoding libraries it takes about 350 MB. Installing it does not start it.
tv.cannot.noInstaller: Hata can install Kodi only on systems with apt. Install Kodi manually and come back.
tv.switchHint: On: Kodi takes over the screen now and after every boot of the server. Off: the screen shows the system console again.
tv.onScreen.kodi: The player has the screen: films, music and photos, driven by the remote on this page or the one in your hand.
tv.onScreen.browser: A web page has the screen. The player is put aside meanwhile and comes back when the page is closed.
tv.onScreen.off: The system's console has the screen: the server's own text terminal, as without Hata.
tv.page.title: Web page on the screen
tv.page.lead: Any web page shown on the whole screen: a dashboard, a camera, a site. The player is put aside while it is there; a film goes on from where it stopped afterwards. Click with an air-mouse remote or a mouse plugged into the server.
tv.page.needs: Shows any web page on the whole screen: a dashboard, a camera, a site. It needs a browser (Chromium) and Cage, a small program that puts one window on the screen with no desktop around it — about 300 MB together.
tv.page.hint: The remote's “home” button gives the screen back too. Sites that protect their video (Netflix and the like) do not play in this browser.
tv.page.full: The video on the whole screen
tv.page.previewFull: This picture on the whole screen of this device
tv.marks.none: None yet. A page kept here is one press away, and a tile on the screen's own page — within reach of the remote.
home.linkScreenHint: A press shows the page on the screen plugged into this server instead of opening it here.
tv.marks.homeDone: “{name}” is on Home: one press shows it on the TV.
tv.marks.name: Name
tv.marks.nameHint: Left empty, the site's name stands for it.
tv.marks.twice: There is a bookmark with this address already.
tv.marks.onScreen: The bookmarks are also tiles on the screen's own page — the one the Browser button opens — so the remote reaches them.
error.tv.noVideo: No video was found on the page on the screen.
tv.page.previewHint: The screen as it is now. A click here is a click there; the wheel scrolls the page.
tv.onScreen.dark: The screen is off: the server sends it no picture, a TV goes to standby. Choose Kodi or the browser to turn it on again.
tv.darkLead: The server sends no picture. Turn the player on to watch.
tv.page.homeHint: Pages are sent here from Hata: Integrations → TV

tv.api.lead: Other programs can put things on the screen: Home Assistant showing the camera when the doorbell rings, for one. tv.api.more: Also: GET {now} — what is on the screen; POST {play} with {"url": …} — a video or a stream in the player; POST {remote} with {"action": "playpause"} — a button of the player's remote.

tv.resolutionHint: A new resolution is applied for {n} seconds: confirm it on the screen or on this page, otherwise the previous one returns. It cannot be changed while something is playing.
tv.matchHint: While a film plays, the screen switches to the film's frame rate, so motion is smooth; afterwards it switches back. The screen goes dark for a moment at the start and at the end.
tv.keepLead: The screen mode has changed. If the picture is there and looks right, keep it; otherwise the previous mode returns in {n} s.
tv.keepGone: Not confirmed: the previous screen mode is back.
error.tv.asking: A new screen mode is waiting to be confirmed. Keep or revert it first.
error.tv.badPicture: The screen does not support this mode.
error.tv.picturePlaying: Something is playing. Stop it first: changing the mode blanks the screen and shows a confirmation over the picture.
error.tv.answerOnScreen: Kodi did not accept the answer from this page. Answer on the screen itself, with the remote.
error.tv.notKept: Time ran out before the confirmation: the previous screen mode is back.
tv.browserHint: Continued from the TV at the same position. No sound or no picture? A browser plays fewer formats than the player: send it back to the TV.
tv.browserCannot: This browser cannot play this file. Playback stays on the TV.
tv.key.textHint: Type into the text field open on the screen
tv.textLead: The text goes into the field currently open in the player on the screen: a search, a name, a password.
tv.textLead.page: First click the field on the page (in the picture of the screen, or with the remote), then type here: the text goes where the cursor stands there — a search, a sign-in, a password.
tv.browserFrom: Continued from the TV at the same position, with the same audio track and subtitles.
tv.channelsHint: The speakers connected to the screen or the receiver. Audio with more channels is downmixed.
tv.passthroughHint: For a receiver or a soundbar that decodes Dolby and DTS itself. Most TVs cannot: leave it off for them.
tv.languageHint: Languages other than English are downloaded by the player from the internet as a language pack on first use.
tv.languageBusy: Downloading and applying the language pack…
tv.languageFailed: The language was not changed: the player could not download the language pack. Try again, or choose the language on the screen in the player's own settings.
tv.audioLanguageHint: The audio track a film starts with when it has several.
tv.saverHint: What the screen does after the player has been idle.
tv.sleep: Turn the screen off when idle
tv.sleepHint: After this long with nothing playing and no button pressed the picture output is switched off, so the TV or monitor goes to sleep. Any button of the remote, or of the remote on this page, wakes it.
tv.inBrowserLead: Videos opened in Files or moved here from the TV play in Hata's own player: you can choose the audio track and subtitles, and audio a browser cannot play by itself (Dolby, DTS) is converted. It works with the TV module off too. The video stream is sent unchanged, so a video codec the browser does not support still will not play.
tv.inBrowserNeeds: With FFmpeg installed, videos opened in Files or moved from the TV get a choice of audio track and subtitles, and audio a browser cannot play by itself (Dolby, DTS). Without it the browser plays only what it supports.
error.tv.badSetting: The player has no such setting or value.
error.tv.languagePlaying: Something is playing. Stop it first: changing the language reloads the whole interface on the screen.
error.tv.noStreams: FFmpeg is not installed. Install it in Computers → This server → Software and updates.
error.tv.notMedia: This file could not be read as a video.
tools.ffmpeg.what: Converts video on the fly so that a browser can play it, with a choice of audio track and subtitles.
media.needs: With FFmpeg installed you can choose the audio track and subtitles here and hear audio a browser cannot play by itself (Dolby, DTS).

tv.link.subsHint: Optional: a subtitle file (vtt, srt) that belongs to this video.
tv.link.noTv: The player on the TV is not running or no screen is connected, so the link cannot be sent there.
tv.link.noBrowser: Playing a link in the browser needs FFmpeg: install it in Computers → This server → Software and updates.

schedule.timedLead: Work Hata starts by itself every day, by the server's clock ({zone}). Work that starts within an hour of other work it gets in the way of is marked.
schedule.repeatLead: Looks that come round by themselves, without a time of yours. Light ones: nothing stops or slows.
schedule.what.backups: Snapshots of the apps, then of the server itself and the second copy. Running apps are stopped for their snapshot.
schedule.what.update: Installs a new version of Hata: Hata restarts, and whatever it is doing then ends.
schedule.what.images: Updates the running apps whose images have newer versions: each one is restarted.
schedule.what.snapraid: Brings the parity up to date with the data disks; it reads them all.
schedule.what.proxmox: Backups of its guests: the work runs on that server, not here.
schedule.scrub: on Sundays also a check of the data
schedule.clash: Starts {minutes} min after «{other}» ({time}), which may still be running.
schedule.clashSame: Starts at the same minute as «{other}» ({time}).
schedule.why.update: The restart of Hata would end the other one.
schedule.why.disks: Both read the same disks: each goes slower.
schedule.why.apps: Both stop and start the apps.
schedule.repeat.hataCheck: Whether there is a new version of Hata
schedule.repeat.trash: What has lain in the trash long enough
schedule.repeat.certificates: Whether a certificate is due to be renewed

power.sleep.title: Sleep when idle
power.sleep.lead: A hard disk that is not read or written stops spinning after this wait: quieter, cooler, a few watts less. The first read after it waits some seconds while the disk spins up.
power.sleep.saved: Saved and given to the disk
power.sleep.failed: The disk did not take it: {message}
mounting.needs.hdparm.why: It tells a hard disk how long to wait idle before it stops spinning, and asks whether it is asleep without waking it.
power.night.title: Off at night
power.lead: The server shuts down at a time and switches itself on again by its own clock. Apps, the backups and the rest stop meanwhile; computers with Hata's client and Proxmox go on as they are.
power.waiting: Waiting for running work to end first: {what}. After two hours it gives up for tonight.
power.hint: Switching on by the clock needs the computer's firmware (BIOS/UEFI) to allow it — often called "RTC wake" or "Resume by alarm". Try it once with the button below before relying on it. Work that runs at a time set for the night does not run while the server is off.
power.cannot.noClock: This computer has no clock with an alarm Hata can set: so it is in most virtual machines and containers.
power.cannot.notRoot: Hata does not run as root here and cannot set the clock's alarm.
power.cannot.readOnly: The clock's alarm cannot be set from here: the system's /sys is read-only (a container).
power.test.button: Try it: off now, on in 3 min
power.test.title: Shut the server down now?
power.test.lead: Hata sets the clock to wake the server in 3 minutes and shuts it down. If it does not come back, the firmware does not allow waking by the clock: switch it on with its button and look for "RTC wake" in the BIOS.
power.test.gone: The server is shutting down; it should be back in a few minutes
power.drawTitle: What the processor and memory draw
power.drawLead: By the processor's own counters (RAPL): the processor and, where it counts it, the memory. The disks, the board and the power supply are not in it — a socket meter shows more.
schedule.what.power: The server shuts down and wakes by its clock: whatever runs then ends.
schedule.whileOff: On the days the server shuts down it is off then ({off}–{wake}): this does not run.
error.power.sameTime: Off and on cannot be at the same time.
error.power.cannot.noClock: This computer has no clock with an alarm Hata can set.
error.power.cannot.notRoot: Hata does not run as root and cannot set the clock's alarm.
error.power.cannot.readOnly: The clock's alarm cannot be set from here.
